name: MapDB
tagline: Embedded Java database exposing concurrent Maps, Sets and Queues backed by disk or off-heap memory.
description: MapDB, by Jan Kotek, is an embedded storage engine for the JVM that hands you familiar java.util collections (HTreeMap, BTreeMap, sets, queues) persisted to a file, to memory-mapped storage or to off-heap memory outside the garbage-collected heap. It grew out of the JDBM project in 2012, and the 3.x line is written in Kotlin and Java. Optional write-ahead-log transactions, snapshots, entry expiration with size or time limits and overflow from memory to disk make it popular as a local cache, an off-heap buffer or a simple embedded key-value store. The last feature release is 3.1.0 (January 2024); 2026 commits on the 3.1 branch only pin dependencies and patch CVEs, so treat it as stable but in maintenance.
statusNote: Last release 3.1.0 (Jan 2024); 2026 activity is dependency pinning and CVE fixes on the 3.1 branch, with no new feature releases.

pricing.notes: Free; the author has offered paid support.

scale.notes: Single JVM; stores can grow to large files on disk.

strengths: Drop-in persistent replacements for java.util Map, Set and Queue
Off-heap storage keeps large data out of GC pressure
Expiration by time or size plus disk overflow for cache use
Single dependency, Apache-licensed, widely used in JVM projects
weaknesses: No feature release since January 2024; maintenance-only
Transactions are optional and limited; no query language or secondary indexes
Historic format changes between 1.x, 2.x and 3.x complicate upgrades
useCases: Local persistent caches and off-heap buffers in Java services
Embedded key-value storage in desktop or Android apps
Spilling large in-memory collections to disk
notIdealFor: Workloads needing SQL, secondary indexes or strong durability guarantees
